stories.head: Consumers use AI agents to recover money from ignored charges
stories.plain: New Use.AI research shows consumers are deploying AI agents to file and win billing disputes that they previously ignored. For marketers, this signals that automated complaint pressure is rising sharply, forcing brands to rethink retention, refund policy, and how AI-driven customer actions show up in revenue models.

stories.head: Salesforce research: AI adoption rises while mobile-worker turnover hits 66%
stories.plain: With 95% of organizations adopting AI but two-thirds reporting higher mobile-worker turnover, Salesforce's Taksina Eammano argues the last-mile delivery experience is broken. The gap between AI investment and frontline outcomes is a real governance and customer-engagement problem brands must solve now.

stories.head: Harris Poll 2026 Holiday Edit: Shoppers cutting spend while keeping traditions
stories.plain: A 1,906-person Harris Poll survey finds US holiday shoppers are selectively trimming budgets rather than abandoning celebrations. Marketers need to adjust seasonal personalization and channel mix now, as spend patterns and format preferences are shifting in ways that affect how AI-driven campaigns should be tuned this quarter.

stories.head: IAB unveils framework for measuring AI's part in conversions
stories.plain: The IAB has released a common standard for deciding how much credit AI gets when it influences or closes a sale. This matters enormously for how budgets get justified and how platforms get paid. Without a shared measurement language, every vendor defines AI-assisted conversion differently — making ROI comparisons nearly impossible. Industry-wide attribution standards like this reshape buying decisions.

stories.head: Marketers deploying AI agents faster than they can measure them
stories.plain: A new report finds most marketing teams are rolling out AI agents without being able to tie those agents' conversations to actual campaigns or revenue. Deployment is outpacing governance and measurement, which means budget decisions are being made blind. This signals a coming correction — either in how agents are built or in how martech stacks are instrumented.

stories.head: Meet your new teammate: Building marketing workflows around AI agents
stories.plain: Coverage from the November MarTech Conference on how to design workflows that blend AI agent efficiency with human oversight and quality control. It offers practical guidance on where human judgment must stay in the loop and where agents can run freely — directly shaping how marketing teams hire, train, and govern AI.

stories.head: Connecting with shoppers when the buyer is not human
stories.plain: As AI shopping agents increasingly make purchase decisions on behalf of consumers, brands face a new challenge: your catalog must appeal to an algorithm, not just a person. The piece explores how to structure product data, pricing signals, and relationship touchpoints so that AI buyers choose you — a fundamental shift in how personalization and CEP strategy get designed.

stories.head: Scrunch launches Citation Optimization to help brands influence sources behind AI recommendations
stories.plain: Scrunch (a Sitecore company) released a tool that maps which third-party publishers and reviewers shape AI-generated recommendations, then helps brands earn citations from those sources. This is a concrete, productized approach to Generative Engine Optimization — making it one of the first tools that lets marketers systematically manage their brand's visibility inside AI answers rather than just search results.

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Workflow Before Anyone Can Measure Them
body: Marketing teams are embedding AI agents into live campaigns at a pace that outruns any governance or measurement framework — agents now draft, schedule, optimize, and in some cases buy media without a human in the loop. Tools like Constant Contact Catalyst, Nectar's always-on creator agent, and DomoAI's one-sentence video agent signal that autonomous execution is the new default, not an experiment.

The danger is a measurement gap that compounds over time: if you cannot attribute what an agent did, you cannot learn from it or hold it accountable. The IAB's new attribution framework and the MarTech cross-channel measurement guide both flag this as the field's most urgent structural problem — speed of deployment & speed of accountability are on completely different clocks.
ev: MarTech · Building workflows around AI agents

themes.head: MCP Connectors Are Rewiring the Stack in Real Time
body: The Model Context Protocol is quietly becoming the new integration layer for the martech stack. Webflow's MCP Connector for Microsoft Copilot, Iterable's hosted MCP server for Claude & ChatGPT, and AppsFlyer's expanded MCP tooling all dropped in the same week — suggesting vendors are racing to be the contextual data source that AI assistants pull from first.

This matters strategically because MCP shifts power away from point-to-point API integrations toward whoever controls the context window. Platforms that expose rich MCP endpoints will become the system of record inside AI-native workflows; those that don't risk being bypassed entirely by orchestration layers that simply query competitors instead.

themes.head: AI Is Becoming the Buyer — and Brands Aren't Ready
body: Two stories hit simultaneously: consumers are deploying personal AI agents to dispute charges and recover money from brands, while on the sell side, Optimove's research shows AI agents are increasingly completing purchases on behalf of human shoppers. The customer journey, long assumed to end with a human decision, now frequently ends with an algorithmic one.

This breaks nearly every personalization assumption in the current playbook — an AI buyer doesn't respond to emotional copy, urgency triggers, or loyalty incentives the same way a person does. Brands that haven't started thinking about machine-readable offers & agent-legible value propositions are building campaigns for an audience that is shrinking.

themes.head: Attribution Is Broken at the Foundation for AI-Driven Media
body: The IAB's new framework for measuring AI's contribution to conversions, the debate over ChatGPT traffic quality versus Google's, and new thinking on combining Marketing Mix Modeling with post-purchase surveys all point to the same rupture: last-click & platform-reported metrics are structurally blind to AI-influenced paths. Cheap CAC looks great in dashboards but hides poor lifetime value when the acquisition channel is an AI recommendation surface.

Building a credible measurement stack now requires layering at least three methodologies — MTA, MMM, and direct-survey attribution — because no single signal is reliable across AI-mediated touchpoints. Marketers who don't rebuild this infrastructure in 2026 will be flying blind into a media landscape where AI intermediaries control an ever-larger share of the funnel.
ev: MarTech · ChatGPT paid traffic vs Google

themes.head: The Hidden Cost of Automation Is Institutional Expertise
body: As AI handles more execution, the craft knowledge that made marketers effective — audience intuition, copy judgment, channel strategy — is quietly atrophying inside teams. The Agile Brand essay on hidden costs and the Forrester SaaS disruption analysis both argue that outsourcing cognition to AI creates a dependency that compounds: the less humans practice a skill, the less they can audit or override the machine when it's wrong.

The strategic implication is a talent and org-design decision, not just a tool-adoption one. Companies need explicit policies about which capabilities stay human-owned & practiced even when an AI can do them faster — otherwise the competitive moat they think they're building is actually a capability gap accumulating beneath a polished dashboard.

month.takeaway: Every theme this month converges on the same asymmetry: AI is moving faster on execution than humans are moving on governance, measurement, and skill-retention — and the gap between those two speeds is where strategic risk is quietly accumulating.
